newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Commerce plans more trade trips.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce plans more trade trips.

text.p: Following a Latin American trade mission next month, U.S. Commerce department plans trade missions to Canada, India, Southeast Asia and possibly Eastern Europe during the rest of the year, Commerce Secretary William Daley said on Wednesday.
The trade mission to Canada would target small to medium sized businesses seeking to develop trade, Daley said after addressing a U.S. Chamber of Commerce conference on Latin America.
He did not say when the trade missions would be scheduled.

Daley is scheduled to leave May 10 on a trade mission to Brazil, Argentina and Chile. The trip is part of the Clinton Administration's efforts to liberalize trade in the region and expand the NAFTA trade agreement throughout Latin America.

"U.S. producers are complaining of losing former Chilean customers to countries with preferential access in products as diverse as apples, cars, textiles and high technologies," Daley said. "And these companies are beginning to make the logical business response -- where possible, they are sourcing their sales to Chile from Canada, Mexico, Argentina and Brazil, rather than from the United States."
